summary: Lewis County summit on Weyerhaeuser Vail Tree Farm land; 1940s spar tree(s), a 1952 ground cab, now a logging truck turnaround; access by permit.

facts.design: 140-foot spar tree with a platform (one spar tree per the register and FireLookout.com; two per WillhiteWeb); a two-story cab and a 1952 ground cab are also mentioned
facts.status_note: The register says the lookouts are gone. WillhiteWeb says remnants are hard to find and the summit is now a truck turnaround.

staffing.status: occupied in 1952 (Harry Williams); no other staffing dates in these sources

access.note: WillhiteWeb: an access permit is needed to legally visit the site inside the Weyerhaeuser Vail Tree Farm. A motorized permit allows driving to the summit; a non-motorized permit starts at a gate at the end of Pigeon Springs Road.

visit.trail_note: No tower stands to climb. Visitors must hold a tree farm permit; the non-motorized route starts at a gate at the end of Pigeon Springs Road.

events.note: Sources give only the 1940s (decade). The register and FireLookout.com describe a 140-foot spar tree with a platform; WillhiteWeb says two spar trees.
Spar tree abandoned in the 1950s (decade only). WillhiteWeb says it was said to be abandoned in the 1950s.

June 14, 1952 Daily Chronicle item (quoted on the Rex page, cite 3) says Harry Williams is located on Windy Knob; WillhiteWeb (cite 4) quotes an April 29, 1952 Chronicle item naming him as of the Windy Knob lookout
Picture of a ground cab on Windy Knob dated 1952; WillhiteWeb has no date for when the cab was placed
One side of the summit logged around 1995; the summit used as a logging landing
Other side logged around 2010; the summit again used as a logging landing

corrections.why: WillhiteWeb says an access permit is needed to legally visit the site inside the Weyerhaeuser Vail Tree Farm.
The register gives only the 1940s for the spar tree, and FireLookout.com gives the same decade; no source gives a single year.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com describe one 140-foot spar tree with a platform; WillhiteWeb describes two. The register also mentions a two-story lookout with a cab, while WillhiteWeb mentions only a 1952 ground cab picture.

notes_for_editor: Brief status gone is supported. Access was unknown in the brief; sources say a permit is needed. The Vail Tree Farm name comes from WillhiteWeb only. The register's administrator field was not captured by the crawl, so agency rests on FireLookout.com's private timber company line. No source describes remains on the summit.
